page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-96 is an x86_64 architecture compute instance configured with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon cores supporting hyper-threading. The instance provides 624 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 6.5 GB per virtual CPU, along with a shared 38 MB Level 3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX and AVX-512F, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES. The configuration features no local storage and zero bundled GPUs, requiring remote network storage for operational file systems and disk persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate high total throughput across parallelized tasks, backed by robust memory bandwidth that reaches 220.79 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 3917.68 GB/sec in cached scenarios. Stress-ng multi-core evaluation places the instance in the upper 25 percent of tested systems. Conversely, per-core performance remains constrained. Single-threaded benchmarks, including Geekbench single-core and gzip compression, fall into the lower quartile, reflecting the architectural characteristics of older generation Intel Xeon cores. Integer text processing and sequential decompression metrics show corresponding limitations.

The hardware profile offers high multi-threaded core capacity and substantial memory density without requiring specialized accelerator hardware. This balance makes the instance suited for memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as distributed in-memory databases, large Redis deployments, Clang compilation pipelines, and heavy multi-threaded data processing. Conversely, workloads that depend primarily on fast single-threaded clock speed or dedicated hardware acceleration for large language model text generation will encounter performance bottlenecks on this configuration.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-96 is an x86_64 server instance featuring 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical Intel Xeon cores and 624 GB of system memory. Providing 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance offers high memory capacity for data-intensive processing. Hardware features include AVX-512F instructions, a 38 MB L3 cache, and dedicated hyper-threaded execution, while omitting onboard local storage and GPU accelerators. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded CPU output and high uncached memory read bandwidth exceeding 220 GB/sec. However, single-core processing capabilities and single-threaded compression speeds score in the lower quartile due to conservative per-core clock rates. The hardware configuration delivers resource density for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, including large-scale Redis caching tiers, batch analytics, in-memory databases, and distributed software compilation jobs that require extensive system memory without hardware acceleration dependencies.
